newsitem.title: USA: Angeion stock slumps on arbitration award. [CORRECTED 23:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Angeion stock slumps on arbitration award. [CORRECTED 23:05 GMT]

text.p: Angeion Corp shares fell Wednesday after an arbitration decision that awarded Medtronic Inc access to a specific group of Angeion defibrillator product patents.

The arbitrator, in a decision announced Tuesday, found that the patents were covered by a pre-existing 1992 licensing agreement between Medtronic amd St. Jude Medical (corrects from "Angeion and St. Jude Medical Inc."),

Medtronic sought arbitration when St. Jude claimed rights to the patents in the wake of its purchase of Pacesetter Inc in 1995. Angeion signed a cross licensing agreement to Pacesetter in 1993 (corrects from "first sold the rights to Pacesetter.
Angeion said it was not a party to the arbitration proceedings, and therefore is not bound by the decision.

"Angeion may have to pursue negotiations with Pacesetter in order to settle this issue," according to Douglas Eayrs, an analyst at John J. Kinnard & Co. "They may also have to assert legal action against Pacesetter to invalidate the 1993 agreement and protect their patents."

Angeion, which designs and develops medical devices used to treat irregular heartbeats, said Wednesday it will vigorously defend its intellectual property rights through negotiation or by other means.
